title: Device capability manifest
description: What was MEASURED about one device. A camera names the profiles it claims; a camera is routinely wrong about that. A capability that is not `verified` is not a capability, and a `verified` capability with no probe behind it is refused rather than published.

tenantId.description: The tenant the device belongs to. It is never read from a request body; it is a property of the device's registration.

siteId.description: The site the device is installed at. NOT NULL on a physically site-bound record.

deviceId.description: The tenant-scoped key of the device this manifest describes.

probeId.description: The probe run that produced this manifest. It is what a reader checks a capability against, and it is what makes the manifest falsifiable.

probedAt.description: When the probe ran. A manifest with no probe time is a claim.

onvifDeviceId.description: The device's own identifier as it reports it. Not a tenant-scoped key.

state.description: `verified` is the only state that counts as a capability. `unverified` is what the device claimed. `contradicted` is what a probe found when the device said otherwise.

probe.description: What established the state. A verified capability with no probe is a claim, and the manifest refuses to publish it.

detail.description: The probe's own words: the token, the status, the reason.
